text:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: observed sustained p99 spikes for streaming endpoints in eu-west-1 for model luminous-3b-q8. Automated alert triggered at 2026-03-15T10:12:08Z. Current SLO breach: p99 ~ 1.9s (target 0.6s). :warning:

alice_oncall: I'm on it. Can people paste the 1h p95/p99 and a quick sample trace? I'll start the escalation if customer impact is >2 tenants.

bob_infra: grabbing metrics from grafana -> query: `sum(rate(stream_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le,region)`; quick snapshot: p95=410ms, p99=1900ms, 99.9=3400ms for eu-west-1 for streaming routes hitting luminous-3b-q8.

claire_ml: we just had an auto-calibration rollout for the int8 profile (commit: ml/auto-calib/2026-03-15/enable) targeting luminous family in eu regions at 09:58Z. It adjusted per-layer quant scales and enabled aggressive KV packing for activation cache.

alice_oncall: timeline lines up. Did rollout touch the dedicated pools or only hosted?

dave_sre: it hit hosted pools and some dedicated nodes in eu because the profile tag matched both. I'm seeing increased GC/dequant CPU on nodes that have older NVidia drivers. Trace snippet (sample trace id: trace-0f3a):
```
span stream_recv -> 0.8ms
span kv_lookup (miss) -> 4.1ms
span dequantize_layer 23 -> 120ms
span dequantize_layer 24 -> 310ms  <-- huge jitter on a subset of hosts
span token_emit -> 1.2ms
```

emma_prodops: customer-facing impact: Support flags show 6 paying tenants in eu reporting slow streaming or dropped frames since 10:05Z. Two on Dedicated with SLA. Fay, please confirm.

fay_support: confirmed, we have support tickets from TenantA and TenantC (Dedicated). TenantA is seeing interactive assistant sessions stall for ~5-8s intermittently. We've opened priority channels.

alice_oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) Rollback the auto-calib profile (slow to propagate), 2) Route new streaming traffic to fp16 variant of luminous-3b (fast), 3) Apply per-host driver workaround to reduce dequant jitter (manual). I vote option 2 + start rollback. Who can flip routing?

bob_infra: I can flip routing policy. Command I'm going to run:
```
# switch eu streaming route to fallback_fp16 for luminous-3b
curl -X POST https://internal-controlplane.local/api/v1/routes/switch \
  -d '{"route":"streaming","region":"eu-west-1","model":"luminous-3b","fallback":"fp16","reason":"p99 spike - autopayload calib"}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"
```

incident-bot: Deploy event queued: routes/switch by bob_infra. Waiting for confirmation.

bob_infra: executed, got 202 accepted. Watching deployment.

deploy-bot: Route switch applied to 60% of eu-west-1 traffic at 10:18:42Z. No errors.

alice_oncall: early telemetry after switch: p95=360ms, p99=720ms (improved), but a subset of long-session streams still show >1.2s due to sticky sessions on older hosts. Continue rollout to 100% and evict sticky sessions.

dave_sre: rolling the route to 100% now and initiating gentle connection draining for sessions on old hosts: `drain -region eu-west-1 -tag driver-old -timeout 60s`

claire_ml: while routing change reduces dequant overhead, root cause appears to be quant calibration created more frequent full-KV-evictions for long-context prompts (>4096 tokens) which amplified dequant cost. We'll revert the auto-calib commit and open a canary with conservative per-layer scales.

bob_infra: route switch to fp16 completed at 10:21:10Z. Full traffic in eu now on fp16 fallback. Observed p99 now 520ms and trending down.

emma_prodops: notifying impacted customers: created message in support channel for TenantA and TenantC: short explanation + ETA for resolution.

fay_support: tenants acknowledged mitigation. TenantA reported sessions recovering; they saw one more 4s stall but then resumed normal.

claire_ml: starting rollback job for the auto-calib profile: `POST /ml/calib/rollback` (job id rollback-3b-2026-03-15). ETA ~ 7min to converge region-wide. I'll post logs.

claire_ml: rollback job started, logs: `rolled back 28/28 nodes in eu-west-1`, status: success at 10:29:03Z.

alice_oncall: metrics post-rollback: p95=340ms, p99=430ms, 99.9=720ms. Great. We're out of SLO breach for now. Timeline: breach window 10:12:08Z -> 10:26:30Z (rough).

gary_sales: flagged top 3 enterprise customers who reported incidents; need postmortem + customer message. Assigning to emma + claire.

emma_prodops: will draft a customer-facing summary: what happened, impact, remediation, and compensatory credit ask. Claire, can you provide a short root-cause paragraph for the draft?

claire_ml: root cause blurb: "An automated calibration rollout for the int8 quant profile increased per-layer dequantization variance on a subset of eu hosts and changed KV eviction behavior for long-context workloads, causing CPU-side dequant jitter and repeated cache misses that amplified tail latency. Rolling back the profile and switching affected traffic to an fp16 fallback mitigated the spike."

alice_oncall: action items (owners):
- claire_ml: fix auto-calib gating and add canary with long-context eval set (owner: claire_ml)
- bob_infra: add routing quick-toggle runbook and automated sticky-session eviction (owner: bob_infra)
- dave_sre: patch driver detection & mark old-driver hosts for rolling upgrade (owner: dave_sre)
- emma_prodops + fay_support: customer communications and SLA review (owners: emma_prodops, fay_support)
- alice_oncall: write incident summary and link logs (owner: alice_oncall)

fay_support: creating support postmortems and will attach logs and sample trace ids to tickets.

dave_sre: protip: add a streaming tail alert that combines p99 and bursty 99.9 for long-context sessions to catch calibration fallout faster.

alice_oncall: agreed. I'll open a follow-up ticket and schedule a 1hr root-cause sync with ML+SRE+Infra tomorrow. Thanks everyone, we'll keep the channel open for updates. :thumbsup:
